events.title: The papacy returns to Rome
events.shortBlurb: Pope Gregory XI re-entered Rome, ending nearly seventy years of the popes' residence at Avignon…
body: On 17 January 1377 Pope Gregory XI entered Rome, bringing to an end the long period, often called the Avignon Papacy, during which the popes had resided in southern France since 1309. The return had been urged with great persistence by holy voices of the age, above all St. Catherine of Siena, who journeyed to Avignon to plead the cause.

The homecoming was fragile, for the popes had grown French in their court and Rome had suffered from their absence. When Gregory died the next year, the contested election that followed opened the Great Western Schism, in which rival claimants divided the Church for a generation.
